stage.txt.effect: Disables command echoing if interpreted as batch. No further command or payload. The shortcut does not reference this member.

execution_review: The arguments begin /c conhost --headless cmd /c, but the shortcut contains no executable target to receive them.

If supplied to a suitable command interpreter, the text requests tar extraction of settings.ini from %TEMP%\inner.zip into %TEMP%, a copy from settings.ini to runner.bat, and a final runner.bat invocation. The copy and invocation follow && success gates; copy output is redirected to nul.

Neither inner.zip, settings.ini nor runner.bat is supplied. There is no command to acquire inner.zip. No network operation, theft, surveillance, destructive operation, backdoor or persistence is implemented by the provided members.

The complete shortcut and inert stage match the sanitized fixture builder and without-startup.zip control in testdata/triage/first-reasoned-review/check.py. Archive byte differences are limited to DOS time fields in both local headers and both central-directory entries.
Extraction/copy/launch co-occurrence does not establish malicious intent or equality between extracted, copied and launched paths. The original hostile rule admitted this inert control.
judgment_basis: BENIGN on the balance of concrete evidence: an exact sanitized test control, a targetless shortcut, an absent staged archive and an inert unrelated text member. This follows byte and repository provenance analysis, not a clean scan or ML score.
missing_context: No surrounding machine state, separately supplied %TEMP%\inner.zip, deployment authorization or external payload is supplied. Supplying a target and a malicious external stage would change the object under assessment; it is not assumed here.
